claims.arxiv2609_02350: A multimodal-language-model agent for continuous vision-language navigation can get around unseen environments efficiently using nothing but a single forward-facing colour camera, ordinary offline expert supervision, and no auxiliary spatial model. Supported only if it beats the strongest earlier agent working under the same resource constraints on both success rate and success weighted by path efficiency in unseen environments, while staying under 24 GB of peak inference memory and running with lower per-step latency than that comparator. It fails if the advantage needs extra training data, richer sensors, external spatial tools, or more memory than that.
claims.arxiv2609_02350_c1: A navigation agent trained only on the standard continuous-navigation datasets carries over to a different navigation task and dataset, and to a physical robot in a workspace it has never seen, without any real-world fine-tuning. Supported only if it exceeds the strongest earlier system under the same transfer conditions on both success rate and path-weighted success, and succeeds in more than half of physical-robot trials, counting a trial successful only when the robot stops within one metre of the instructed target.

0.text: Build the agent and its supervision. Setup: start from an 8B vision-language model and train one epoch at learning rate 1e-5 using only the expert trajectories of the two standard continuous-navigation datasets. At every expert step, supervise a single sequence containing the progress label, the predicted outcome for each candidate action, the decision whether to write the observation into memory, its role label, and the ground-truth next action; all the non-action labels are generated by deterministic rules over the trajectory with a five-step lookahead, with no extra environment rollouts or manual annotation. Memory is a fixed queue of length 8. About 1,000 GPU-hours on eight A100s.

1.text: Navigation in unseen environments under the resource constraints. Setup: evaluate on the unseen validation splits of two datasets, measuring navigation error, oracle success, success rate and path-weighted success. Result: on the first dataset, 5.34 error, 55.9 oracle, 49.7 success, 45.3 path-weighted, against 5.95 / 55.8 / 44.9 / 30.4 for the comparator that matches the constraints, namely single-camera with no auxiliary module and no extra data. On the second, 6.89 / 46.9 / 39.9 against 8.79 / 36.7 / 25.5. Two stronger-looking systems do not meet the constraints: one uses an external spatial tool and reaches 52.8 success and 49.2 path-weighted, and two others use 10M and 12.6M extra training examples. Comparator numbers are taken from their own papers rather than rerun.

2.text: Does it stay inside the stated resource envelope? Setup: run the unseen split at memory queue lengths 4, 6, 8 and 10, recording success and peak GPU memory, plus per-step latency at the default. Result: success 48.9%, 48.3%, 49.7% and 49.3% with peak memory 18.9, 19.2, 19.7 and 20.3 GB, so every setting stays under the 24 GB ceiling. Per-step latency at the default length is 59 ms against 194 ms for the external-tool system, which also needs 44.3 GB.

7.text: How much of the headline result comes from training on the second dataset as well? Setup: train one model on the first dataset alone and one on both, then evaluate both on the first. Result: 6.61 error / 40.3 success / 36.5 path-weighted for the single-dataset model against 5.34 / 49.7 / 45.3 for the joint model. So 9.4 of the success points come from including the second dataset, which is within the claim's 'standard datasets' allowance but means the single-dataset agent would not clear the comparator.

8.text: Does it transfer to a different navigation dataset and task? Setup: evaluate on the unseen split of an object-goal navigation benchmark. Result: 38.0 success and 26.9 path-weighted, against 35.2 / 19.6 and 37.1 / 19.8 for the two published comparators, so it leads on both measures, with the larger margin on path efficiency.

9.text: Does it transfer to a physical robot? Setup: deploy the simulation-trained agent unchanged on a wheeled robot with a front-facing camera and a 24 GB GPU, in a workspace it has not seen. Ten instructions involving visually similar objects and behaviours such as entering and leaving rooms, each repeated three times, counting success when the robot stops within one metre of the target. Result: 21 of 30 trials, a 70% success rate.

notes: Nearly the whole paper was visible at 18 pages. [1] now separates comparators that meet the resource constraints from those that do not, which is the whole point of C0's bar and was flattened in v3. [7] now quantifies how much of the result depends on the second training dataset and notes that the single-dataset agent would not clear the comparator.
